process.title: How commercial document attestation works
process.intro: The steps below are an overview based on the document’s place of issue. A specialist should confirm the exact route before you proceed.
process.foreign: If your document was issued abroad
foreignSteps: Check the document and arrange verification or notarisation with the relevant authority in its country of issue, where required.
Complete the home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation, where applicable.
Arrange attestation by the UAE Embassy in that country.
Complete the final UAE MOFA attestation, where required.
process.uae: If your document was issued in the UAE
uaeSteps: Arrange the required verification or signing through the relevant UAE court, Chamber of Commerce or free-zone authority.
Submit the document for UAE MOFA attestation, where applicable.
Arrange attestation by the embassy of the destination country, if required.

faq.title: Commercial document attestation FAQs
items: It is the process of obtaining the required verification, attestation or legalisation for a business document so it can be presented to an authority or organisation. The exact route depends on the document and destination.
Which business documents may need attestation?

Examples include a Memorandum of Association, trade licence, board resolution, certificate of incorporation, commercial power of attorney and other company records. Confirm the requirement with the receiving authority.
What is the process for a document issued abroad?
It may involve verification in the issuing country, that country’s foreign affairs authority, the UAE Embassy there and final UAE MOFA attestation. The exact sequence must be checked for your case.
What is the process for a UAE-issued document?
Depending on the document, verification may be required through a UAE court, Chamber of Commerce or free-zone authority, followed by UAE MOFA and the destination country’s embassy where applicable.
How long does commercial attestation take?
A standard turnaround has not been supplied. Timing depends on the document, country, authorities and any additional requirements. Ask for a case-specific estimate.
Is UAE MOFA attestation always mandatory?
Not necessarily for every use case. The receiving authority and destination determine which attestations are required. Confirm the current requirement before starting.
Why might a company need to attest its documents?
A bank, government department, business partner or overseas authority may request authenticated company documents for a particular transaction or application.

An apostille is a form of authentication used between participating countries under the Hague Apostille Convention. Whether it is accepted depends on the countries and receiving authority. Verify the current route officially.
Do you offer document pick-up and delivery?
The business states that free pick-up and delivery is available within the UAE. Confirm service availability for your location and document before arranging collection.
The confirmed country list has not yet been provided. Share the country of issue and destination so the team can check the route.
How can I get a quote?
Send the document type, country of issue, destination country and any deadline through WhatsApp or the contact form. The team can confirm the applicable steps and quote.
Can I track the progress of my documents?
Contact the team to confirm what progress updates are available for your specific case.

preparation.title: Prepare your commercial document enquiry
preparation.intro: A few details can help the team understand which attestation route may apply. You do not need to guess the legal requirements before speaking with a specialist.
paragraphs: Start with the country where the document was issued and the country where it will be presented. These details help identify which authorities may be involved. If a bank, government department or business partner requested the document, ask them whether they have a specific format, validity period or wording requirement.

Identify the exact document name. A Memorandum of Association, a trade licence and a board resolution are different records, and the receiving organisation may ask for one document or several. If the name on the document differs from the name used in your request, explain that difference when you contact the team.

Keep the original document and any supporting records available. Do not alter, laminate, bind, translate or send an original until the relevant authority or service team confirms what is required. The supplied process summary is a starting point only; the correct requirements must be checked for the issuing authority and destination.

If you are handling documents for a company, be ready to explain your role and whether you are authorised to submit them. Share only the information needed for an initial enquiry. Avoid sending confidential financial or corporate records over an unsecured channel before the team confirms a suitable submission method.
